item.title: bcup2kdbx: a security audit, a fix, and my vault converted
item.author: emecas
item.description:
Yesterday I wrote about moving from Buttercup to KeePassXC, and ended with bcup2kdbx ★ star note, a community tool that converts a Buttercup vault into a KDBX database: “It’s third-party and new, so check it before you use it.” So before giving it my vault, I checked it, and fixed what I found along the way. Then I converted my vault.

What I wanted to know

Two things: that it doesn’t reach the Internet while it runs, and that it writes nothing anywhere except the output file I name.

item.title: Moving from Buttercup to KeePassXC: not by choice, but by necessity
item.author: emecas
item.description: For a long time Buttercup was my password manager. It was simple, open source, and it fit the way I worked. So when its maintainer, Perry Mitchell, announced on March 3, 2025 that the project was ending, it wasn’t something I could ignore. He explained that since co-founder Sallar left, he had been the only active maintainer, and that the project’s scope, across operating systems, mobile platforms and third-party services, with ongoing security requirements, was too much for one person. On June 26, 2025 the desktop app’s repository was archived and is now read-only, like the rest of the project.

item.title: Measuring and improving the quality of my notes
item.author: emecas
item.description: This blog started as a text file. For more than ten years I kept short notes in one file, Index.txt, in a Git repository: a title, a link, sometimes a line or two about why it mattered. Later came notes from the repositories I star on GitHub, from issues I open as reminders, and from articles. Today there are 1,432 of them on this site, and more are coming: I have more than 20 other data sources still to process and include, such as bookmarks, podcast notes, notes on my favorite blogs and the books I read.
